The same AgentSpace and the same capability services the Java annotations
bind, as decorators, dataclasses, and plain functions
(`L3L4-COVERAGE.md` §6.4). An `@entry` class names its wire schema; a
`Space` holds the layer-3 verbs; a `Template` carries the Java matchers
(`eq`, `ne`, `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`, `in_`, `contains`, `is_null`,
`not_null`, or any callable) over fields and tags; `watch` delivers
`WRITTEN`, `TAKEN`, and `COMPLETED` once per entry; `TakeContext.current()`
is the take a worker runs under.

```python
from agentspaces.space import Space, Template, entry, gte
from agentspaces.agents import Binder, agent, ballot, bid_function, on_decision, on_estimate, space_notify, space_take

@entry("ai.badmonkey.agentspaces.examples.fleet.ResearchFleet$ResearchTask#v1")
@dataclass
class ResearchTask:
    topic: str
    priority: int

@agent("researcher", description="Researches topics", goals=["research"])
class Researcher:
    @space_take("tasks", lease="30s", where={"priority": gte(1)})     # take, call, complete with the result
    def research(self, task: ResearchTask) -> Finding: ...

    @space_notify("tasks")                                            # once per entry, never consuming it
    def audit(self, finding: Finding) -> None: ...

    @bid_function("tasks")                                            # the AUCTION price
    def price(self, task: ResearchTask) -> float: ...

    @ballot("votes", prefix="council:")                               # one ballot per proposal, None abstains
    def judge(self, proposal: Proposal) -> str | None: ...

    @on_decision("votes", prefix="council:")                          # once, when the quorum closes it
    def record(self, decision: Decision) -> None: ...

bound = Binder(peer, agent=identity.renewing_subordinate("py-worker", "PT24H")).bind(Researcher())
```

`Binder.bind` runs the loops the Java `AgentBinder` runs: one thread per
take, reactions off the delivery thread, the ballot cast once per proposal,
the decision once at quorum, and the AgentCard (name, description, goals,
consumes, produces, space bindings, declared actions, the agent certificate)
published on the `ads` stream on bind. `vote.propose`, `vote.cast`, and
`vote.decision` are the procedural forms; the tally rule is Java's.

The return conventions are the Java binder's (ISSUE-WorkflowVerbs,
ISSUE-Motion): `None` writes nothing; `Tagged(value, {"region": "eu"})` is
written with its tags; a list or tuple is the fork, each element written on
its own after the take completes; a `Motion(proposal_id, question, options,
quorum, space=None)` opens a vote once per proposal id in its space or the
binder's `vote_space`. Two more cues: `@propose(space, vote=..., options=...,
quorum=..., prefix=..., key=[...])` opens a vote from a cue once per key (the
method returns the question, `None` to ask nothing, or a `Motion`), and
`@space_join(space, key=..., parts=[Part(Fraud), Part(Coverage), Part(Claim,
optional=True)])` is the LOCAL join: once per key, when every required part
is readable, the method receives a `Joined` (`key`, `get`, `find`, `all`,
`has`). The fleet-wide LEASED and ORDERED join modes, `@SpaceReduce`, and
the decorated `@OrderedTake` need the ticket and the Raft voter and are not
here; an ordered take runs through `Space.take(template,
through=OrderedLog(Pipes(peer)))` instead (below).
`Space.entries(template)` is the metadata view (`Entry`: `entry_id`,
`value`, `tags`, `issuer`, `expires_at_millis`, `taken`), and every event
carries its entry's tags. A watch, and `@space_notify(on=[...])`, deliver
five kinds: `WRITTEN`, `TAKEN`, `COMPLETED`, `EXPIRED` (the write lease
lapsed while the entry was open: a leased entry as a timer), and
`REAPPEARED` (a take claim lapsed), the last two judged by a sweep on the
clock, once per entry and lapse. `Space.notify(template, callback, lease)`
is the leased push subscription of the Java space (JS-V-01): it lapses on
the peer's clock unless `renew()`ed, and the binder renews a notify's, a
propose's, and a join part's at half-lease while the agent is bound. Takes
and `read(timeout=...)` wake on folds rather than polling: at most one
anti-entropy pull per settle window, none while folds arrive (JS-V-02).
The decorators and `Part` take `filters=["priority>=3", "region in eu,us"]`,
the portable grammar of SPEC §7.2, beside the `where` matchers (JS-V-03).
A `Contribution(epoch, value)` return
starts the epoch on the binder's aggregate, and `produces=[...]` on a take or
notify names the card's produced types when the return annotation does not. Maps a signature covers (`tags`, `costHints`,
`spaceBindings`) are sorted by `cbor.canonical_map` (wire version 3).

`agentspaces.capabilities` speaks the layer-4 pipes (`PIPE_DATA` frames
addressed to a member): `Aggregate` (push-sum `avg`, roster `sum` and
`count`, `min`, `max`, `estimate`, `Settle`, `await_settled`, `on_estimate`,
and the `@on_estimate` decorator), `Semantic` (the hashing embedder with
Java's `String.hashCode` so the vectors agree, `query`, `remote_query` over
the query pipe, and answers to other members' queries), and `remote`
(`actions` from the cards the `ads` stream carried, `invoke` through the
task space with the shared-fields correlation), and `OrderedLog` (the Raft
client of `aspace:cap/ordered-log`, JS-V-05: `take` submits a signed
`ClientSubmit` claim command to the leader the advertisements name, or to any
reachable member that forwards it under its leader hint, and holds the entry
once the committed claim folds back from the space; the Raft frame union and
the ClientSubmit are pinned by the golden `raft_*` vectors), and `connect`
(the agent side of the connector protocol, JS-C-14: `DataQuery`,
`DataResult`, `AssetChange`, `AssetInvocation`, and `AssetInvocationResult`
as `@entry` dataclasses in Java record order, pinned by the golden
`data_query_cbor`, `data_result_cbor`, `asset_change_cbor`,
`asset_invocation_cbor`, and `asset_invocation_result_cbor` vectors, with
`canonical_hash` agreeing with `DataQueryEntries.canonicalHash`;
`DataQueryClient.fetch(asset, parameters, timeout)` pull-once by canonical
hash, a live result under the hash answering at once and a `DataQuery`
written otherwise, counting `cache_hits` and `queries_sent`;
`connect.invoke(space, card, operation, params, timeout, invocation_id=None)`
writing an `AssetInvocation` and returning the `AssetInvocationResult` the
card's issuer writes, the same `invocation_id` on a retry so the target runs
once; `asset_cards(peer, asset=None)` and `invoke_ops(card)` over the ads
stream; a result counts only from the named `trusted_connectors`, the
caller's own `trust(issuer_peer, asset)` rule, or, for an invocation, the
card's issuer; readers drop fields they do not know, JS-F-06; the connector
runtime itself stays in Java and TypeScript). MAJORITY_GOSSIP
is `vote.cast_preference` and `vote.leader` over the aggregate's push-sum
shares (JS-V-04), the epochs Java's `VoteCapability` names. A dial-only peer
sends frames to its seed directly and to every other member through it: the
seed carries a `RELAY_FRAME` when it holds the `RELAY` role (SPEC §5.4), and
the peer's `relay.via` hint tells members to reach it the same way back. Not here: the Raft voter (JS-F-18), so reduces and
the fleet-wide LEASED and ORDERED join modes; the gossip-learning exchange
(its payload is encoded and golden-pinned); and every transport but tcp and
tls (the client skips `ws`, `wss`, `http`, `https`, `webrtc`, and `dtls`
endpoints, JS-N-05 as amended on 2026-11-03).

**TLS.** A `tls://host:port` seed, or `peer.connect(host, port, scheme="tls")`,
dials TLS 1.3 and presents a channel certificate: a fresh P-256 key in a
certificate the peer's Ed25519 identity key signs, with the identity key in
the CN (SPEC §5.6, `agentspaces/tls.py`, mirroring Java's
`ChannelCertificate`). The peer attests the seed the same way from the
certificate it presents and refuses one that attests nobody, so a Java node
built with `requireAttestation(true)` admits it. On an attested connection it
announces `CHANNEL_HELLO` once, so a Java node in ATTESTED or SESSION mode
stops signing every frame toward it, and it accepts the bare frames that
follow from exactly the attested sender (`peer.attested_frames`); it keeps
signing what it sends. Seeds are `Seed(host, port, scheme)` tuples
(`agentspaces/seed.py`), and `connect_any`, `bootstrap`, and `join_invite`
dial `tcp` and `tls` seeds in priority order. `tests/test_tls.py` pins the
binding against a Python TLS seed, and `CouncilCrossLanguageTest` runs this
worker over `tls://` against a Java council that requires attestation. No
session resumption and no early data, so every attestation rests on a full
handshake; the standard library reads a certificate chain from files only, so
the key and certificate pass through an owner-only temporary directory at
each dial.

`demo_council_worker.py` is the whole of it against the Java
`CouncilFleet` coordinator: tasks taken, the council ballot cast, the epoch
contributed to, the semantic query answered, the remote action served.
`tests/test_layer34.py`, `tests/test_layer4.py`, `tests/test_verbs.py`,
`tests/test_verbs_residency.py` (JS-V-01, JS-V-02, JS-V-04, the mixed-scheme
fleet), `tests/test_ordered.py` (JS-V-05 against a simulated log), and
`tests/test_connect.py` (JS-C-14 against a simulated connector: the golden
bytes, a query answered and the identical one served from the space, a
result accepted only from a trusted connector, an invocation answered only
by the card's issuer, a retry that never runs the target again) prove each
piece without a socket; `tests/workers/ordered_worker.py` is the worker the
Java `PythonOrderedTakeTest` spawns against three Java voters,
`tests/workers/connect_worker.py` the one `PythonConnectorClientTest`
(agentspaces-connect-core) spawns against a Java `ConnectorRuntime`, and
`tests/workers/content_worker.py` the one `PythonContentClientTest`
(agentspaces-content) spawns against a Java relay and a Java mirror.

## Large artifacts: the content swarm

`agentspaces.capabilities.content` is `aspace:cap/content-swarm` (SPEC
v0.1.23 §7.1, §8, annex G): an artifact of any size is hashed in fixed
pieces, its signed `Manifest` (a CIDv1 root) and each holder's leased
`Holding` live in the group's `content` space, and the pieces move from
every holder at once, verified before they are stored or served.

```python
from agentspaces.capabilities import Content, FileStore, Pipes

content = Content(Pipes(peer), Space(peer, "content"), FileStore("/var/lib/aspace/content"))
content.run()                                   # ticks the scheduler on a thread
manifest = content.publish("weights.bin", name="weights.bin")   # bytes or a path
fetch = content.fetch(manifest["root"])         # from the seed and, through it, every other holder
if fetch.wait(600):
    data = fetch.read_bytes()                   # or content.store.read_all(root)
print(fetch.progress(), fetch.trace[-3:], content.describe(manifest["root"]))
```

A `FileStore` resumes after a restart and republishes what it holds; a
`MemoryStore` is for tests. With a `Content` attached, every `Space` over
the peer escalates a payload above `escalate_above` (4 MiB) to an artifact
and one above 64 KiB to a block, and a read of either kind of entry returns
it once its bytes are here (`Peer.payload_of`: never a block on the
network). A holding's `via` names the relay a holder sits behind; the
scheduler orders sources by hops. `tests/test_content.py` pins the golden
vectors and runs the swarm in process.

## Application cards: origin, formats, and the spill

An `AppCard` (SPEC v0.1.32 §6.1a.2 to §6.1a.5) says how an app connects in
`kind` (`peer`, `fed`, `gateway`, or `assembled`, a static app served as is),
where it came from in `origin`, and which media types and vocabularies it
reads or renders in `formats`. No kind is tied to an origin. `wire.app_card`
builds one in Java field order, and the peer applies the AppCard level and the
spill when it publishes:

```python
from agentspaces import wire

origin = wire.app_card_origin("realm", "example-realm/example-app", "",
                             {"realm.reads": "Item,Order", "realm.format": "1",
                              "realm.namespace": "urn:realm:example-realm#"})
card = wire.app_card(peer.group, peer.identity, "example-app", issued, kind="fed", shape="static",
                     url="https://apps.example.org/example-app.html", origin=origin,
                     formats=["text/html"], host=wire.app_card_host("https://apps.example.org", published_at_iso=issued))
issued_card = peer.publish_ad("AppCard", card)       # the card as signed
found = [a for a in peer.app_cards() if wire.from_origin(a, "realm", "example-realm/*")]
full = peer.resolve(found[0])                        # a stub's parts, fetched from the content swarm
```

The peer advertises `wire.appcard=2`. While any member of its view is below
level 2, it signs each card without `origin`, `formats`, and an `idp` host, and
it reissues its cards at once when the view's level changes. A card whose
encoding passes 65,536 bytes travels as a stub when the whole view is at level
2 and a content swarm is attached: its `reads`, `actions`, `views`, and `ui`
(an AgentCard's `actions` and `ui`) move into a parts document, and `resolve`
fetches it. The peer logs a warning once a card passes 57,344 bytes. The
advertisement cache holds at most `ad_cache_max_entries` (8,192)
advertisements of every kind and `ad_cache_max_bytes` (32 MiB) of their
encodings. The counters
`app_cards_downgraded`, `cards_spilled`, `cards_oversize_inline`,
`ads_refused_cache_full`, `spills_refused`, and `spills_over_limit` show each
case. A `Binder` given `data_use_type` writes each `@data_use` declaration as
an entry of that type into `data_use_space`, and writes nothing without one.

## Values that change: persistent data trees

`agentspaces.pdt` is the Python port of the persistent data trees
(srad/agentspaces-pdt.md, PD-C-04): content-addressed values whose every
version shares the nodes it did not change, so a member that holds one
version fetches only the delta of the next. The layouts match the Java
build byte for byte, and `tests/test_pdt_vectors.py` proves it against every
`pdt_*` and `content_*` tree vector of `golden.json`.

- `PMap` and `PSet`: a CHAMP trie with sha256 key hashing; a key set reached
  in any order has one root. `get`, `assoc`, `dissoc`, `update`,
  `update_in`, iteration, `count`, `diff`, `merge3`, equality by root.
  A value that is itself a `dict` is embedded in the order you built it,
  while the Java codec sorts a map's keys (ISSUE-CanonicalMaps), so put a
  nested dict in canonical order (`cbor.canonical_map`, or build it with its
  keys sorted shorter-first then bytewise) when its root must equal Java's;
  scalars, strings, byte strings, and lists need nothing.
- Escalated space payloads (PD-E-01, PD-E-03): a `payloadRef` whose CID is
  dag-cbor names a persistent tree a Java writer escalated into; the peer
  hands it to the facade (`Pdt.payload`), which reassembles the bytes once
  the tree is here and starts one tree fetch otherwise, so an entry of an
  opted-in space reads as any other. `write_payload` and `read_payload` in
  `agentspaces.pdt.values` are the Java `PayloadTree` byte for byte
  (`tests/test_pdt_payloads.py` pins the Java roots).
- `PVector`: Clojure's tailed trie; `conj` and `pop` rewrite the root alone
  until the tail fills or empties.
- `PBlob`: FastCDC chunks (16/64/256 KiB) under a prolly tree; `read`,
  `append`, `splice`, and `PBlob.of` over bytes, a path, or a stream. An
  insert of 100 bytes into an 8 MiB blob rewrites about one chunk (median
  79 KiB in the test).
- `NodeStore`: nodes by CID in memory or one file per node, with pins,
  `complete`, `missing`, `reachable`, and a mark and sweep.
- The tree exchange (`agentspaces.pdt.tree.Trees`): tags 8 to 11 of the
  content swarm, the holder side and the fetcher, holdings for tree roots,
  the `trees` parameter on the advertisement, and `group-key` sealing of
  `NODES` answers when the peer holds the content key.
- Refs (`Pdt`, `Ref`): `deref`, `swap`, `watch`, `history`, `at`, and
  `heads` over `PRef#v1` entries in a space, with the key-wise three-way
  merge of several heads (the later HLC wins a both-side conflict and a
  `PConflict` says so), inline deltas on the head up to 32 KiB, and linear
  mode over the space's take, as the Python `@reduce` path works.

```python
from agentspaces.capabilities import Content, MemoryStore, Pipes
from agentspaces.pdt import Pdt, NodeStore, PBlob

content = Content(Pipes(peer), Space(peer, "content"), MemoryStore())
pdt = Pdt(content, Space(peer, "pdt"), NodeStore("/var/lib/aspace/pdt"))
pdt.run()                                        # ticks the exchange and the refs on a thread
facts = pdt.map_ref("facts")
facts.swap(lambda m: m.assoc("alpha", 1).assoc("beta", [1, 2, 3]))
print(facts.deref().to_dict(), facts.heads()[0].seq)
facts.watch(lambda value: print("new head", value.count()))
facts.on_conflict(lambda c: print(c.reason, c.key))
log = pdt.vector_ref("log", mode="linear")       # one writer at a time, through the take
blob = PBlob.of("/data/model.bin", pdt.store)    # chunk a file; pdt.trees.hold(blob.root()) serves it
```

A reader that lacks a head's root fetches the delta against the versions it
holds (`follow="full"`, the default) or loads nodes on access
(`follow="lazy"`). The ref space is an ordinary replicated space: a head is
a signed, leased entry with the tags `name` and `root`. A Python writer
renews its live heads at half-life and cancels each superseded head of its
own two seconds after a newer head replaced it (`Peer.cancel_entry`), unless
a fork still walks through it. The peer
advertises the `wire.recordless` hint and accepts a renew, cancel, or
complete without its record (SRAD §3.9). `tests/test_pdt_swarm.py` runs two
peers in process: a delta fetch with a held base receives exactly the
delta, a swap derefs on the other peer from the inline delta, and a 100-key
concurrent swap converges on both; `tests/workers/pdt_worker.py` is the
peer a Java cross-language test drives over tcp.

### PDT 2: feature level 2

The client reads every PDT 2 form (srad/agentspaces-pdt2.md, P2-C-01), so its
content-swarm advertisement carries `pdt = "2"` beside `trees = "1"`. It
sends a level-2 form only to a member whose advertisement carries level 2.

- Heads: `PRef.v` 1 and 2. A head over a tree that holds a text, or another
  level-2 kind, is version 2.
- `pdt.db_ref(name).deref()` gives a lazy `DbReader` (`datoms`, `entity`,
  `lookup`) of a DataScript database. DataScript writes the ref.
- `PText` (`agentspaces.pdt.text`): a text that merges by Fugue's rules.
  `insert`, `delete`, `merge`, and `with_replica`; a map value of text spills
  to a `t` node above 1 KiB, and two writers' texts in one key merge by union.
- `PVector` reads a relaxed (`rr`) vector that another port spliced, and
  `packed()` gives its `vr` form. A write packs it first.
- `PBlob.open_verified(offset, length)` delivers each 16 KiB group only after
  it verifies against the blob's BLAKE3 identity through its Bao outboard
  (`pdt.blake3`, `pdt.bao`).
- Every head names its `vg` node (`pdt.ancestry`), and a merge walks the
  chain past versions whose entries are gone.
- The tree exchange applies `NODES.deltas` (zstd frames; Python 3.14's
  `compression.zstd`, else the chunk travels whole), answers `CHALLENGE`, and
  reconciles held roots by negentropy or RIBLT (`Trees.reconcile_held`).
- `Pdt(..., push=True)` takes pushed deltas from `pdt:<space>:<name>`.
- `content_store.Stores` reads `content-store` cards and writes `SignedPin`
  entries (`store_for`, `receipts`).
